why: A campaign reference for turning user data into culturally recognizable, shareable visual assets while keeping the brand flexible across genres, markets, social formats, and out-of-home moments.

compositions.title: Personal data as campaign creative
compositions.study: The campaign converts individual listening behavior into a branded story people want to publish themselves.
compositions.reuse: Use when a product has personal usage data that can become a respectful, opt-in visual artifact.

compositions.title: Social-first format family
compositions.study: Bold color, type, and shape systems survive stories, feeds, outdoor placements, and editorial coverage.
compositions.reuse: Design the smallest shareable unit first, then scale up to launch pages and public media.

assets.notes: Each asset needs strong first-frame hierarchy and enough brand signal after platform compression.
assets.reuse: Create templates that can ingest data while preserving brand rhythm and legibility.

assets.notes: Messaging works because it feels specific to the user while belonging to a global campaign.
assets.reuse: Let variables alter the story but keep the grammar recognizable.

motion.title: Sequential personalized reveal
motion.notes: Motion can turn metrics into a paced celebration rather than a static report card.
motion.fallback: Every animated card should export as a legible static share image.

interactions.title: Built-in distribution moment
interactions.study: The campaign succeeds because the visual asset and the sharing behavior are designed together.
interactions.reuse: Design campaign visuals alongside their sharing, download, and embed paths.

implementation.notes: Useful for year-in-review, usage recap, community benchmark, and personalized product storytelling.

capture.attribution: COLLINS Spotify case study and It's Nice That Spotify Wrapped identity coverage
